blocks.speaker: narrator
blocks.text: Jesus was on the road again, moving through Jericho with his disciples and a large crowd. Everywhere he went, people followed him.

verses.text: And they came to Jericho: and as he went out of Jericho with his disciples and a great number of people, blind Bartimæus, the son of Timæus, sat by the highway side begging.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: And they came to Jericho: and as he went out of Jericho with his disciples and a great number of people, blind Bartimæus, the son of Timæus, sat by the highway side begging.

blocks.speaker: narrator
blocks.text: Bartimæus could not see the crowd, only hear it. He sat in his usual place beside the road, begging for what little people might spare. Most days, people walked right past him without stopping.

blocks.speaker: narrator
blocks.text: Then he heard who was passing by. He had never seen Jesus's face, but he knew enough to hope. He did not wait for someone to notice him.

verses.text: And when he heard that it was Jesus of Nazareth, he began to cry out, and say, Jesus, thou Son of David, have mercy on me.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: And when he heard that it was Jesus of Nazareth, he began to cry out, and say,

segments.speaker: bartimaeus
segments.text: Jesus, thou Son of David, have mercy on me.

blocks.speaker: narrator
blocks.text: Perhaps the people thought a beggar had no business calling out to a teacher. Perhaps they just wanted to keep moving. Bartimæus knew this moment would pass in seconds, and he might never get another one.

verses.text: And many charged him that he should hold his peace: but he cried the more a great deal, Thou Son of David, have mercy on me.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: And many charged him that he should hold his peace: but he cried the more a great deal,

segments.speaker: bartimaeus
segments.text: Thou Son of David, have mercy on me.

blocks.speaker: narrator
blocks.text: A crowd can be loud enough to drown out one voice. Yet Jesus heard him. In the middle of all those footsteps and talking people, Jesus stopped walking.

verses.text: And Jesus stood still, and commanded him to be called. And they call the blind man, saying unto him, Be of good comfort, rise; he calleth thee.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: And Jesus stood still, and commanded him to be called. And they call the blind man, saying unto him,

segments.speaker: crowd
segments.text: Be of good comfort, rise; he calleth thee.

blocks.speaker: narrator
blocks.text: The same people who had told him to hush were now telling him to get up.

verses.text: And he, casting away his garment, rose, and came to Jesus.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: And he, casting away his garment, rose, and came to Jesus.

blocks.speaker: narrator
blocks.text: He threw off his cloak so nothing would slow him down, and found his way by the sound of the voices.

blocks.speaker: narrator
blocks.text: Everyone there could guess what a blind beggar wanted. Even so, Jesus did not assume. He asked, and gave the man room to speak for himself.

verses.text: And Jesus answered and said unto him, What wilt thou that I should do unto thee? The blind man said unto him, Lord, that I might receive my sight.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: And Jesus answered and said unto him, What wilt thou that I should do unto thee? The blind man said unto him,

segments.speaker: bartimaeus
segments.text: Lord, that I might receive my sight.

blocks.speaker: narrator
blocks.text: He did not ask for silver. He asked for the one thing he could not give himself.

verses.text: And Jesus said unto him, Go thy way; thy faith hath made thee whole. And immediately he received his sight, and followed Jesus in the way.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: And Jesus said unto him, Go thy way; thy faith hath made thee whole. And immediately he received his sight, and followed Jesus in the way.

blocks.speaker: narrator
blocks.text: Notice what he did next. Jesus told him to go his way. And Bartimæus chose to walk down the road behind Jesus. The man who had sat blind in the dust beside the road was now walking on it, seeing clearly, following the one who had stopped for him. That is the quiet truth the story leaves with us. No crowd is too loud, and no person at the edge of the road is too small, for Jesus to stop and listen.
